[USER] User is trying to get more organized with snack planning.  
[USER] User wants help to come up with a weekly snack schedule to prep healthy options on the weekends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Having a weekly snack schedule can help with healthy eating and reduce unhealthy impulse snacking.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Sample weekly snack schedule provided:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Monday**:  
- Morning: Fresh fruit (e.g., apples, bananas, berries)  
- Afternoon: Nuts and seeds (e.g., almonds, cashews, pumpkin seeds)  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Tuesday**:  
- Morning: Yogurt parfait (Greek yogurt, granola, berries)  
- Afternoon: Carrot sticks with hummus  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Wednesday**:  
- Morning: Energy balls (oats, nuts, dried fruit)  
- Afternoon: Hard-boiled eggs  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Thursday**:  
- Morning: Cottage cheese with fruit (e.g., berries, sliced peaches)  
- Afternoon: Raw veggie sticks with guacamole  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Friday**:  
- Morning: Smoothie packs (frozen fruit, spinach, protein powder)  
- Afternoon: Trail mix (nuts, seeds, dried fruit)  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] **Weekend Prep**:  
- Cut fresh fruit (e.g., apples, carrots, bell peppers)  
- Prepare energy balls or granola bars  
- Boil eggs  
- Assemble yogurt parfaits or smoothie packs  
- Portion out nuts, seeds, and dried fruit  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips and variations provided for the snack schedule:  
- Rotate snacks every 2-3 weeks to keep things interesting.  
- Consider dietary needs and preferences when selecting snacks.  
- Incorporate seasonal fruits and veggies.  
- Prep extra snacks on the weekend for busy weeks.  
- Involve family members or roommates in the snack prep process.
